review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Some people believe that advertising brings good effects to economy, while others think society has been badly affected because it can make people disappointed with who they are and what they have. There are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

On the one hand, admittedly, advertising can brings undeniable economic benefits. People who agree with this opinion say that creative content and appealing visual effects often stimulate consumer demand. In this way, spending power will be increased, leading to more productions are encouraged to buy. This naturally follows that more employment opportunities and greater state revenues through taxation, resulting in a stronger economy. For instance, e-commerce platforms such as Shopee or Lazada in VN rely heavily on advertising campaigns to attract consumers, boosting not only their sales but also the entire digital retail sector. In addition, advertising creates jobs in marketing, media and design, which is an important driver of economic activity.

On the other hand, people disagreeing say advertising has negative social consequences. This is primarily because it constantly shows images of perfect lifestyles, beauty standards, or luxury possessions, causing to foster dissatisfaction among viewers. In particular, young people often feel impressed to buy trendy clothes or the latest smart gadgets advertised on TikTok, leading to frustration when they cannot afford them. In this sense, advertising promotes materialistic values and money-driven culture in the long run.
Overall, I am convinced that each view valids to some certain extent. Advertising contributes to social dissatisfaction, while playing a crucial role in economic development.

Tuy nhiên, bài còn nhiều lỗi cơ bản như “can brings”, “more productions are encouraged to buy”, “causing to foster” và “each view valids”. Viết xong, em chưa tự kiểm tra và sửa lỗi cẩn thận. paragraphs: The news media brings too many impacts on how people live now and this is an adverse development. Personally, I believe that media really affects society, but it is not fully bad.

Admittedly, news media has too many effects on people's lives. This is primarily because the widespread access to smartphones and the Internet, those technologies allow people to follow the news instantly. This means that wherever and whenever they are, news has become a regular part of their routine. Beside that, the intense competition among news outlets, in order to gain attention, leads to that most media agencies often focus on shocking and breaking content and present it in a highly sensationalized manner. In this way, with dramatic headlines and eye-catching visuals, it reinforces the overall impact of news on public opinion.

Despite that, news media brings lots of positive effects. It exposures to a certain stream of distressing and exaggerated new, leading to overwhelm people and make them feel overly anxious and helpless, even in situation that do not directly affect them. However, news coverage also warn the public to existing and looming problems in society, such as crime, natural disasters, or political corruption. This naturally follows that individuals can be better informed and more prepared to respond to potential threats, actually resulting in it can handle risks in an increasingly complex society.
In conclusion, although it is true that news media may bring about a few disadvantages to people, however, I am convinced that it is not really bad.

paragraphs: It is argued that news media has a substantial impact on how people live now and that this is an adverse development. Personally, I believe that media really affects society; however, this influence is not entirely negative.

Admittedly, news media has a substantial influence on people's lives. This is primarily because the widespread access to smartphones and the Internet allows people to follow the news instantly. This means that wherever and whenever they are, news has become a regular part of their routine. Besides that, the intense competition among news outlets means that, in order to gain attention, most media agencies often focus on shocking and breaking content and present it in a highly sensationalized manner. In this way, presentation with dramatic headlines and eye-catching visuals reinforces the overall impact of news on public opinion.

Although news media can have harmful effects, it also brings positive effects. Exposure to a constant stream of distressing and exaggerated news can overwhelm people and make them feel overly anxious and helpless, even in situations that do not directly affect them. However, news coverage also warns the public to existing and looming problems in society, such as crime, natural disasters, or political corruption. This naturally follows that individuals can be better informed and more prepared to respond to potential threats, thereby helping these individuals handle risks in an increasingly complex society.
In conclusion, although it is true that news media may bring about a few disadvantages to people, I am convinced that its substantial influence is not entirely negative.

paragraphs: Some argue that students who have the best academic performances should been rewarded, while some others say that rewarding students who show their advancements is more necessary. From my perspective, both of these types of students are worthy to get reward in educational environment.

Admittedly, rewarding students who have excellent results is a evident. This is primarily because these students have diligently applied themselves to their study so they deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, leading them to be propelled toward overall academic gains. Beside that, the kind of competition has been seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Therefore, students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, helping enable the to achieve success in later life.

However, I strongly believe that students having improvements also should been rewarded. The fact that only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, causing others to think that their effort is fully futile. Given they can not surpass those outstanding individuals, they are prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened. This naturally follows that those students gradually lose the incentive to study. Otherwise, emphasising improvements can encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. In this way, the constant desire to outdo themselves can benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am convinced that rewarding students who show the best academic results or improvements brings positive values, more confident to learn in studying.

paragraphs: Some argue that students who have the best academic performances should be rewarded, while some others say that rewarding students who show their advancements is more necessary. From my perspective, both of these types of students deserve rewards in an educational environment.

Admittedly, rewarding students who have excellent results is justified. This is primarily because these students have diligently applied themselves to their studies, and thus they deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, leading them to be propelled toward overall academic gains. Besides that, the kind of competition has been seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Therefore, students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, enabling them to achieve success in later life.

However, I strongly believe that students who show improvement should also be rewarded. The key reason is that if only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, this can cause others to think that their effort is futile. Given that they may feel unable to surpass those outstanding individuals, they are prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened. It naturally follows that those students gradually lose the incentive to study. By contrast, emphasising improvements can encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. In this way, the constant desire to outdo themselves can benefit students more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am convinced that rewarding students who show the best academic results or improvements brings positive values.

Tự sửa từ nối theo quan hệ thật: Besides là bổ sung, By contrast là đối chiếu, It naturally follows that là kết quả.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: In some nations, parents decide to educate children themselves at home instead of allowing them to go to school. In this essay, however, I am to refute this school of thought.

Initially, parents who apply home school also have their reasons. This allows parents to save money because no school fees are required. Moreover, home-educated children are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure. both, which cause emotional and mental problem. Added to this is that parents teaching their children at home by themselves can tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones. That is often not the case in traditional schooling because of the large class size.

However, I believe that the substantial detriments of this opinion can outweigh the positive. Firstly, this educational approach not actually save money, since parents need to pay a large amount of money for lab equipment and tutors. Therefore, one parent needs to be cut off and cater for their child's needs, be these academic or personal. Secondly, most parents are not well versed in all school subjects, leading to difficulties in properly explaining concepts for children and ultimately academic problems. Finally, even social problems that children can be faced with at school, such as bullying or having romantic feelings for others, it often help them prepare for social and workplace situation in the future.
In conclusion, although it is true that a this problem brings some benefits, these are relatively minor and should not over shadow the far more significant and long-lasting drawbacks it entails.
review.overall: Em viết đủ bốn đoạn, nêu ba lợi ích và ba nhóm bất lợi, rồi kết luận hại lớn hơn. Tuy vậy, mở bài 'I am to refute this school of thought' chưa trả lời phép cân lợi–hại và chưa có view cụ thể để bác; câu mở Body 1 'parents who apply home school also have their reasons' đã gợi nhóm phụ huynh theo cách học này nhưng chưa nêu rõ lập luận ba lợi ích. Body 2 có khung phản biện nhưng 'Therefore' nối sai quan hệ chi phí với thời gian chăm con. Em còn lỗi câu nền ở 'approach not actually save', 'both, which', 'it often help' và dùng từ nối ngoài khung văn viết đã học. Cần viết lại các câu này bằng cấu trúc đã học, rồi tự soát từng chủ–vị và quan hệ ý.

paragraphs: In some nations, parents decide to educate children themselves at home instead of sending them to school. Personally, I believe that the disadvantages of homeschooling outweigh its advantages.

Supporters of homeschooling argue that this approach offers several benefits. Firstly, this allows parents to save money, as no school fees are required. Moreover, home-educated children are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, both of which can cause emotional and mental problems. Added to this is that parents teaching their children at home by themselves can tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones. That is often not the case in traditional schooling due to large class sizes.

However, I believe that the substantial drawbacks of this approach outweigh its benefits. Firstly, this educational approach does not actually save money, since parents need to pay a large amount of money for lab equipment and tutors. One parent may also need to reduce working hours to cater for their child's needs, be these academic or personal. Secondly, most parents are not well versed in all school subjects, leading to difficulties in properly explaining concepts to children and ultimately academic problems. Finally, even social problems that children can be faced with at school, such as bullying or having romantic feelings for others, can help them prepare for social and workplace situations in the future.
In conclusion, although it is true that this approach brings some benefits, these are relatively minor and should not overshadow the far more significant and long-lasting drawbacks it entails.
